Subject: Next steps: local SDK onramp, auth & routing checklist

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard + proposed next steps so your engineering team can get a local proof-of-concept running this week.

What we heard (recap)
- Primary goal: fast local integration to validate embeddings + a lightweight reranker before committing to dedicated capacity.
- Constraints: air-gapped staging for initial tests, on-prem model routing for regulated workloads, SSO-backed key management in prod.
- Success criteria: embedding similarity within expected ranges on 10k docs, <120ms median token latency on short prompts in local env, and deterministic reranker reproducibility on stable prompt set.

Immediate technical asks we captured
1) Python + TypeScript quickstart repos for local testing (we're attaching a zip with both).
2) Recommended env matrix (Python 3.10/3.11, Node 18 LTS) and minimum GPU/CPU spec for representative runs.
3) Auth/routing options: API key for POC, SSO + KMS for later stages, and policy-based routing to fall back to smaller/quantized variants when latency budgets hit.
4) Embeddings + reranker approach: provide sample embedding index and an example reranker prompt + eval harness.

Proposed next steps (actionable)
- Today: I attached redwood-local-sampleapps-v1.zip — unpack and run README-local.md in the Python folder. That will run a small embedding ingestion and local rerank test.
- Wed/Thu: 30-minute technical deep-dive with Karthik to walk through auth wiring and on-prem routing logic. Availability: Wed 1/21 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 1/22 14:00-15:00 PT.
- By EOD Friday: your team shares a short test set (500 docs) so we can validate embedding parameters and give a recommended quantization/profile for your workload.

Attachments: redwood-local-sampleapps-v1.zip (Python/TS quickstarts), nimbus-arch-notes.pdf (notes from call)

If that plan looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive and Marissa will coordinate trial credits/HubSpot next steps.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Elena —

Great questions. Short answers below, plus I’ve looped in Karthik for the TS/function-calling sample and proxy notes.

1) Reranker approach - For the POC we recommend a prompt-based re-score using the same base open model (faster iteration) with an optional lightweight learned reranker later once you lock the objective. This avoids extra training overhead while you calibrate similarity thresholds.

2) Proxy / air-gapped staging - The quickstart supports HTTP(S)_PROXY env vars. For stricter air-gapped installs we provide a downloadable model artifact and an on-prem runtime package (separate Private deployment plan). If you need, we can send a small VMware/OCI image for an isolated runner.

3) SOC 2 / audit evidence - Our security team owns SOC 2 evidence. I’m adding Marissa to coordinate — she’ll share the SOC 2 kit and an evidence onboarding contact.

TS function-calling & structured output - Karthik, can you attach the minimal TS sample that demonstrates tools + structured JSON outputs and a short note about embedding integration?

Proposed calendar: I’ll send a Wed 10:00 PT invite for a 30-minute technical workshop (Karthik + 2 devs from Nimbus). If that time doesn’t work, we can do Thu 2:00 PT.

Deliverables we’ll produce right after the deep-dive:
- a concrete quickstart runbook for Python and TS with exact env vars and example prompts
- an embedding sample set (500 docs) with a scoring baseline and reranker template
- a one-page ops note on routing policies and fallback models for predictable latency

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Jonas

Hi Elena —

Quick technical checklist / notes for your engineers before the workshop. I included minimal snippets in-line; full samples are in the Drive link Jonas shared.

Local env (recommended) - Python: 3.10 or 3.11, pip, venv - Node: 18.x LTS, npm/yarn - OS: macOS/Linux (Ubuntu 22.04), Windows WSL2 supported

Env vars
- REDWOOD_API_KEY (for POC; rotate for production)
- HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY if behind proxy
- REDWOOD_REGION (us/eu) to pin routing during tests

Python quickstart (high level) - pip install redwood-sdk - python quickstart/run_local.py --seed 42 --docs sample_docs/500.jsonl
- The script builds embeddings and does a simple linear rerank, then a model re-score pass. Look at config.yml to toggle quantization profiles.

TypeScript quickstart (function/tool calling + structured output)
- npm install @redwood/inference
- In examples/ts/tool-calling.ts:
  const response = await client.chat.create({
    model: 'redwood-llama-2-13b',
    messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Extract invoice metadata and return JSON schema'}],
    tools: [invoiceParser],
    structured_output: {schema: 'invoice_v1'}
  });

- The structured_output block returns a JSON payload that your downstream processors can validate against a schema. We recommend using the parser hook to normalize dates and currencies before indexing.

Embedding + reranker tips
- Use 1536-dim embeddings for semantic search at POC scale; store in Faiss/HNSW with L2 or cosine.
- For reranking, keep the candidate pool to 50-200 for lowest latency. Prompt-based re-score reduces complexity for first pass.

On-prem considerations
- If strict air-gapped, use our Private runtime tarball and the offline model artifact; we’ll provide an install script to register the runner with a customer-managed control plane.

I’ll bring the TS sample for function-calling to the workshop and walk through the structured_output schema and a small test harness.

If possible, please confirm which two engineers will join Wed 10:00 PT so I can tailor the demo.
